reuse.why: The change reuses RSchedule, recurrence conversion, date utilities, and the existing weekend-adjustment helper, although schedule assembly remains repeated.

duplication.why: The range handler repeats the upcoming handler's recurrence construction and conditional occurrence adjustment instead of sharing that orchestration.

placement.why: Holiday and exclusion rules live appropriately in shared/schedules.ts, but the range handler embeds a domain-specific adjustment-distance formula.

scope.why: The changes stay focused on the requested scheduling rules, range endpoint, associated types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Shared adjustment helpers provide a sound foundation, but repeated schedule assembly, untyped configuration inputs, and an unexplained range-margin formula increase maintenance effort.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The new handler and modified consumers call the shared recurrence and weekend-adjustment helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated construction and adjustment in getDatesInRange are direct repetitions rather than disguised implementations.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter and an invalid-mode compatibility branch; recurConfigToExcludedRules introduces a yearly-versus-one-off holiday branch, while consumers continue using the shared helpers.
